question.problem: Which statement correctly describes a **stable** equilibrium point?

choices.value: Solutions starting close to the equilibrium may leave a small neighborhood of it but still converge to it as $t\to \infty .$
No matter how close a solution starts to the equilibrium, it will eventually leave any fixed neighborhood of the equilibrium.
Solutions can converge to the equilibrium only when the system is linear.
Solutions starting close to the equilibrium stay close only for a finite time, then may behave arbitrarily.
Solutions that start sufficiently close to the equilibrium remain close, but do not necessarily converge to the equilibrium.
